Developer authentication

Authentication

To start making calls to Brex APIs, generate a user token from your Brex dashboard and pass it along in your API call headers.

#### 

1. Generate a user token

  1. Sign in to dashboard.brex.com as an account admin or card admin.
  2. Go to Developer > Settings.
     * If your company has not accepted the developer API agreement, please review the terms and conditions. These must be accepted to use the developer API.
  3. Click Create Token.
  4. Create a name for your token that will help you identify it. Choose what level of data access you need for your application; these are the scopes your token will have.
Image: #width=700px;
  5. The next screen will confirm your previous selections. Make sure it looks good, then select Allow Access.
Image: #width=600px;
  6. Your token is now created. Copy and store the token securely. You won't be able to see it again.

## Brex MCP

Early access

Brex MCP lets you connect AI assistants like Claude Code, Codex, Slack, or Cursor directly to your Brex account. Once connected, you can ask your AI questions about your company's spending, cards, and expenses in plain language, without leaving your AI tool.

For example, you could ask:

"What did the engineering team spend on SaaS last month?"

"Show me my bank account transactions from the last week?"

"Show me all unapproved reimbursements over $500."

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open standard that lets AI assistants securely access external tools and data sources. Brex's MCP server uses your existing Brex API credentials and respects the same role-based permissions you've already set up; your AI only sees what your user account is allowed to see.

MCP features

Brex MCP exposes read and write capabilities across core Brex resources. Common use cases include:

#### Expense and transaction analysis

Query transactions, card expenses, and reimbursements with filters -- by date range, merchant, employee, department, compliance status, or spend limit.

MCP security and access control

Brex MCP is available to any Brex account with Developer API access enabled. The AI assistant operates under the permissions of the credentials used to authenticate, and can only access data that the associated user or service account is permitted to view or modify.

If your organization has not yet enabled Developer API access, an admin can do so from Settings > Developer > API.

Two ways to authenticate

  * OAuth: Scopes are handled for you. When you connect, the MCP server requests exactly the permissions its tools require, and you approve them in the authorization prompt. No manual configuration is needed.
  * API token: The MCP server respects the scopes provisioned on the token. If a scope is omitted (for example, cards read), the corresponding tools will be unavailable. The server will never attempt to access resources outside what the token permits. You can generate and scope tokens from Settings > Developer > API.

We recommend granting only the scopes your AI workflow actually needs when using API tokens.

All actions taken via the MCP server are recorded as the MCP client on behalf of the authenticated user when using OAuth.

Getting started with Brex MCP

Full setup instructions including how to configure your AI client, authenticate with Brex, and scope your API token can be found in the developer documentation: Set up Brex MCP.

At a high level, setup involves the steps below:

Prerequisites [Admin only]

  1. Enable early access. An account admin or card admin enables Brex MCP from Settings > Early access in the Brex Dashboard by selecting Brex in AI assistants.
  2. Accept the Developer API agreement. An account admin or card admin accepts the agreement from Settings > Developer.

To connect to the MCP: Follow the steps in the Developer guide to continue setting up.

Supported AI clients

Brex MCP works with any MCP-compatible AI client, including:

Claude Code

Configure via `claude mcp add --transport http brex https://api.brex.com/mcp in your terminal.`

Codex

Configure via` codex mcp add brex --url https://api.brex.com/mcp in your terminal.`

Cursor

Add the MCP server URL under Cursor's MCP settings

Slack

Follow the setup instructions listed here.

More client-specific setup steps are covered in the developer documentation (https://developer.brex.com/docs/mcp).

Former API server URLs

As of January 1, 2026, we are transitioning base URLs to `api.brex.com` and `api-staging.brex.com` respectively, but the former URLs (`platform.brexapis.com` and `platform.staging.brexapps.com`) will continue to be available for the forseeable future.

Production: `https://api.brex.com`

Staging: `https://api-staging.brex.com`

Data in Staging

There are no availability guarantees in staging - data stored in staging environments may be purged at any time. Use staging for point-in-time testing only.

Scopes

`openid`: Required to make an OpenID Connect request.

`offline_access`: Required to obtain an OAuth 2.0 Refresh Token.

The scopes page describes how scopes work in the Brex API and the scopes required for each API.

Brex API FAQ

Brex API FAQ

What is the difference between a user token and an OAuth token?

The user token is used to authenticate your own Brex account. The OAuth token is used when building partner applications to authenticate other Brex accounts.

What is the expiration time for a user token versus an OAuth token?

User tokens expire if they are not used to make an API call for 90 days. When used regularly, they will not expire. User tokens can also be revoked using the Brex dashboard if needed. The OAuth token lasts for one hour and then must be refreshed.

Can a Brex user have multiple Brex deposits accounts and cards?

Yes, a Brex user can have multiple deposit accounts and cards. You can use the List Cash Accounts endpoint to get a list of deposit accounts and the List Cards endpoint to get a list of cards for a user.

Is it possible to get pending transactions via the API?

This is not available through the API today.

Overview

# 

Overview

Copy

Brex is the first fully unified spend platform — with global corporate cards, expense management, reimbursements, travel, and bill pay. Brex makes it easy for finance teams to control all of their spend, all in one place. Using the Brex API, you can power your internal tools and create custom workflows.

Brex APIs use the REST architecture, are defined using the OpenAPI specification and use standard HTTP response codes and verbs. All APIs accept and return JSON and require HTTPS.

Explore our guides and review our API documentation to see how you can integrate with Brex.

  * Accounting API: View and manage accounting data
  * Budgets API: Manage budgets and budget programs
  * Expenses API: View and manage card expenses data, receipt match and receipt uploads
  * Fields API: View and manage fields and their options
  * Onboarding API: Refer your customers and personal contacts to Brex and prefill signup information
  * Payments API: Manage vendors and send ACH, domestic wires, and checks
  * Team API: Manage users, locations, departments, and cards
  * Transactions API: View your transactions, accounts, and statements
  * Travel API: View trips made in Brex Travel
  * Webhooks API: Send real-time notifications based on events

Quickstart

Check out our quickstart guide to get up and running making your first Brex API call in just a few minutes. The rest of the guides and documentation provide more in-depth context.

API Status

Go to https://status.brex.com to see API and Brex system status.
